npc:anastasia-hartwell.text: Anastasia Hartwell. Anastasia Hartwell is a prominent Forsaken mage trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. She guides fledgling and developing spellcasters in mastering the arcane arts and oversees vital magical research and field missions across Lordaeron and beyond. Standing within the dark, echoing chambers of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Anastasia Hartwell instructs Forsaken and Horde mages in channeling arcane energies. Though the kingdom of Lordaeron fell to ruin, former human practitioners like Anastasia have preserved their scholarly traditions in undeath. She maintains that magic demands strict discipline, warning any traveler she meets that careless incantations will quickly consume the untrained. Beyond fundamental spell instruction, Anastasia directs promising students toward vital field investigations. She sends mages to the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades to gather snapdragons that show how far the plague has spread, and into Algernon's alchemist shop in the Apothecarium to capture the invisible creatures of pure magic behind a strange disturbance. Through her tasks, practitioners learn that mastering magic means confronting its dangers directly, even within their own city. Anastasia's connections reach well beyond the borders of Tirisfal. As Horde spellcasters grow in proficiency, she coordinates with fellow trainers in distant lands, such as Deino in Orgrimmar, and directs advanced students toward solitary masters like Tabetha in the swamplands of Dustwallow Marsh. Her guidance ensures that Forsaken mages remain woven into the wider tapestry of the Horde's magical pursuits.

npc:apothecary-johaan.text: Apothecary Johaan. Apothecary Johaan is an alchemist and researcher of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed in Brill. Tasked by his order and Lady Sylvanas, he conducts lethal experiments on local flora and fauna to develop the Forsaken's new plague. Working openly out of the Forsaken settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades, Apothecary Johaan represents the scientific ambitions of the newly formed Royal Apothecary Society. Like his colleagues across Lordaeron, Johaan operates under direct orders to craft biological and alchemical weapons capable of securing the Forsaken's fragile future against the living and the Scourge alike.

npc:apothecary-renferrel.text: Apothecary Renferrel. Apothecary Renferrel is a prominent member of the Royal Apothecary Society stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Tasked with advancing the Forsaken's alchemical endeavors, he coordinates extensive field research into the region's corrupted wildlife and undead threats. Travelers through Silverpine frequently assist him with gathering volatile reagents and investigating dangerous Scourge remnants. Operating out of the Sepulcher, Renferrel serves as one of the Royal Apothecary Society's chief field researchers in Silverpine Forest. While Undercity houses the grand laboratories and high leadership of the society, Renferrel handles the practical, muddy work of securing native biological specimens, refining potent concoctions, and analyzing the grim ecology of Lordaeron's western border.

npc:aramis-hammerhand.text: Aramis Hammerhand. Aramis Hammerhand is an undead holy warrior situated within the desecrated chapel of Deathknell. As a Forsaken paladin trainer, he instructs newly risen dead who seek to reclaim their bond with the Holy Light. Walking this path in undeath requires immense discipline, as wielding such radiant energy inflicts agonizing pain upon their decayed flesh. Standing within the somber walls of Deathknell's chapel, Aramis Hammerhand represents an anomaly among the recently awakened Forsaken. In life, many citizens of Lordaeron answered the call of the Silver Hand, only to perish when the Scourge swept across the north. Aramis survived the fall only to be raised into undeath, yet he chose not to abandon the martial and spiritual teachings of his former existence. Now, he offers guidance to others who refuse to surrender their devotion. For an undead being, channeling the Holy Light is an ordeal of supreme willpower. The power burns necrotic flesh and reawakens long-dead nerves to excruciating pain. Aramis instructs his initiates that holding to this faith requires enduring continual torment. Through tasks like 'A Difficult Path' and 'Rediscovering the Light', he demands that young paladins confront the physical and spiritual costs of wielding a force inherently opposed to their present nature.

npc:arugal.text: Arugal. Archmage Arugal is a former wizard of Dalaran who unleashed the feral worgen upon Lordaeron. Overcome by madness and grief, he now rules from the heights of Shadowfang Keep, treating the savage beasts as his beloved children while menacing all of Silverpine Forest. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Arugal was a member of the Kirin Tor, though some peers like Dalar Dawnweaver dismissed him as a charlatan whose weak spellcraft relied heavily on enchanted trinkets. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Arugal sought a weapon powerful enough to stem the tide. Drawing upon the esoteric research of the late Dalaran mage Ur, Arugal pierced the veil between realms and summoned the worgen into the mortal world. The ravenous beasts tore through the undead legions as intended, but their feral ferocity could not be contained, and their savage hunger swiftly turned against innocent mortals. The summoned horrors slaughtered not only the Scourge but soon turned on the wizards themselves. The beasts then besieged the ancestral seat of Baron Silverlaine, and the keep fell swiftly to claws and fangs, its lord and retainers slain in the massacre. Rather than flee from his monstrous creation, Arugal's mind fractured under the weight of guilt, and he adopted the beasts as his own offspring. Renaming the fortress Shadowfang Keep, Arugal entrenched himself within its ramparts, surrounded by ghostly victims and loyal hound-packs.

npc:baine-bloodhoof.text: Baine Bloodhoof. Baine Bloodhoof is the son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof and the acting protector of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. While his father governs the tribes from the towering heights of Thunder Bluff, Baine directly oversees local defense, investigating encroaching industrial exploitation and defending against feral predators. He serves as an essential bridge between youthful tauren braves and the ancestral wisdom of his clan. Born to Cairne, Baine spent his youth traveling alongside his nomadic people before they claimed the rich grasslands of Mulgore. His early life was marked by the ever-present threat of the centaur clans. Shortly after the Third War, a centaur warband under Khiragg captured young Baine, plunging Cairne into a grief-stricken stupor that nearly shattered the newly founded settlements. It was only through the courage of the champion Rexxar that Baine was liberated from captivity. That rescue restored Cairne's spirit, allowing the tauren to stand with Thrall's Horde against the invading Kul Tirans and secure their foothold on the continent. Rather than lingering in the relative comfort of the capital mesas, Baine chooses to reside among his kin in Bloodhoof Village. As Cairne advances in age, Baine carries an increasing burden of stewardship, representing the next generation of tauren leadership. He directs braves and visiting allies to combat the unruly Palemane gnolls who pester the borders, and keeps a watchful eye on suspicious outside influences threatening Mulgore's natural balance. Beyond territorial border clashes, Baine faces modern encroachers unconcerned with spiritual balance. To the east, the goblin Venture Company cuts deep into the sacred landscape, while dwarven prospectors from Bael Modan dig into ancestral soil at the Bael'dun Digsite. Baine advocates for a firm yet measured response: attempting to warn the miners and destroy their destructive equipment rather than rushing into senseless bloodshed. He warns that the dwarves' violent digging is hurting the spirits of the earth, though the miners refuse to listen.

npc:bethor-iceshard.text: Bethor Iceshard. Bethor Iceshard is a powerful Forsaken mage based in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Presiding over the arcane and shadow practitioners within the Temple of the Damned, he commands considerable authority in Sylvanas's realm. Beneath his chilly demeanor lies a past entwined with old friends torn apart by the Scourge. Standing within the Temple of the Damned, Bethor Iceshard oversees the practitioners of the arcane arts and shadow magic in the Undercity. Respected and feared for his intellect and icy resolve, Bethor wields sufficient political and magical weight to give direct instructions to provincial magistrates across Lordaeron. He directs agents of the Forsaken to secure valuable grimoires, investigate arcane anomalies, and stamp out rival powers that threaten the Undercity's dominion. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Bethor was a mortal apprentice studying magic alongside two close companions: Gunther Arcanus and Thule Ravenclaw. As a testament to their fellowship, the three students wove their practice wands together. The Scourge shattered that bond entirely. When death and dark magic swept across the kingdom, Thule Ravenclaw willfully surrendered his soul to the Lich King, Gunther perished and rose on an isolated island in Brightwater Lake, and Bethor succumbed only to later break free as Forsaken.

npc:brewmaster-drohn.text: Brewmaster Drohn. Above Ratchet's docks, Brewmaster Drohn tends his brewing craft. The orc lives just uphill from the port, making potent drinks with methods tied to the wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout. Travelers who find discarded kegs across Kalimdor are sent to Drohn's porch. Brewmaster Drohn brews from his home on the hill above Ratchet's goblin docks. Rather than devote himself to combat, the orc has given his craft to brewing. He lives peacefully in the neutral haven established by Gazlowe's Steamwheedle cartel. While many orcs favor coarse grog or simple spirits, Drohn works with rare ingredients, carefully balanced flavors, and methods seldom practiced among his kin. Brewmaster Drohn learned brewing through a mentor who studied under Chen Stormstout, the pandaren wanderer who fought beside Rexxar and the Horde during the founding of Durotar. Chen also taught Drohn to make Trogg Ale. When travelers find Chen's discarded kegs in the wilds, Drohn is the only local authority who can identify their ingredients and recreate the wanderer's potent brews.

npc:brine.text: Brine. On Blackthorn Ridge, Brine guides shaman initiates toward the spirits of water. This orc shaman teaches them to commune with the tides and earn their Water Totem. Brine lives on a hill in northern Blackthorn Ridge, far from the Barrens' trading posts. Though dry savannas surround her, she has devoted her life to understanding water. Shaman across the Horde seek her wisdom after mastering earth and fire. She teaches that water calls for patience and perspective, qualities few understand as deeply as she does. In her youth, Brine marched with her orc companions across the Hillsbrad Foothills and fought against human settlements. During the campaign, she came to Tarren Mill and found a humble well fed by fresh spring water. The well stayed in her memory as a sign of life amid devastation. It strengthened a lesson she had learned as a child: even in the darkest sorrow, a small token of hope can still be found.

npc:cairne-bloodhoof.text: Cairne Bloodhoof. Cairne Bloodhoof is the venerable High Chieftain of the united tauren tribes and ruler of Thunder Bluff. A towering warrior of immense wisdom, he bound the fate of the tauren to Thrall's Horde after the orcs aided his people in escaping extinction at the hands of the centaur. For generations, the tauren lived as wandering nomads across the Barrens, continually hunted and driven toward extinction by savage centaur marauders. When Thrall and his orcs arrived on the shores of Kalimdor, Cairne recognized a rare nobility in them. Thrall offered military protection, escorting Cairne's desperate caravan across the plains to the safety of Mulgore in exchange for guidance to the Oracle at Stonetalon Peak. Settling upon the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, Cairne finally established a permanent, unified home for all tauren tribes. Indebted to Thrall, Cairne followed the orcs to Stonetalon Peak and fought side by side with the Horde and Jaina Proudmoore's humans against the Burning Legion during the Third War. Later, when Admiral Daelin Proudmoore invaded Durotar, Cairne personally took up arms once more to fight alongside Rexxar after his captured son, Baine, was safely recovered. Today, Cairne stands as one of the Horde's most respected elders and Thrall's closest confidant, offering calm council against reckless warmongering.

npc:canaga-earthcaller.text: Canaga Earthcaller. In the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller guides new Horde shamans toward the spirits of the land and their first totems. Canaga Earthcaller guides Darkspear trolls and orcs who begin the shaman’s path from the red bluffs of the Valley of Trials. He teaches newcomers to quiet their minds and listen to Kalimdor’s rumblings. They prepare earth sapta so they can commune with the spirits. Canaga asks each novice to gather sacred reagents and travel to the local spirit rock in Durotar. There, they drink earth sapta and see the elemental spirits firsthand. Through his guidance, they earn their Earth Totem.

npc:carendin-halgar.text: Carendin Halgar. Carendin Halgar is a prominent Forsaken warlock trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Sharp-tongued and notoriously short on patience, he oversees the training of fledgling practitioners of the dark arts. He instructs aspiring warlocks on how to subjugate powerful demonic entities from the Twisting Nether, notably teaching the rituals to bind Voidwalkers and Succubi. Within the noxious gloom of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Carendin Halgar instructs those who delve into the Twisting Nether. He demands focus and obedience, holding little tolerance for failure, hesitation, or weakness. Under his watchful gaze, warlocks are pushed beyond basic incantations into the dangerous mastery of summonings and soul manipulation, cementing the Forsaken's ruthless approach to demonic servitude.

npc:chief-hawkwind.text: Chief Hawkwind. Chief Hawkwind is the tribal leader of Camp Narache, the proving grounds nestled in the Red Cloud Mesa of Mulgore. Responsible for guiding the youth of the Shu'halo, he mentors new adventurers as they embark on their traditional rites of passage. Under his watchful gaze, young braves learn humility, respect for the land, and the strength needed to protect their people. Standing at the heart of Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind carries the solemn responsibility of preparing the next generation of tauren for the wider world. Red Cloud Mesa serves as a sheltered haven where fledgling hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors undertake the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. Hawkwind oversees these customs, ensuring that every youth learns duty and endurance before venturing beyond the safety of the mesa. Hawkwind's lessons begin with humility rather than martial glory. He sends initiates on simple chores, such as fetching clean spring water, to instill reverence for the natural world and their elders. Only after demonstrating a humble heart are braves guided toward tests of martial prowess, culminating in trials that test their resolve against the aggressive Bristleback quilboar encroaching upon the ancestral plains. Beyond his role as a mentor, Chief Hawkwind must reckon with rising dangers right at his camp's doorstep. The Bristleback tribe has grown increasingly bold, pressing hard against the perimeter of Red Cloud Mesa. Hawkwind coordinates the defense of the settlement, tasking newly proven braves with blunting the quilboar assaults to ensure the sacred training grounds remain secure.

npc:coleman-farthing.text: Coleman Farthing. Coleman Farthing is a bitter Forsaken survivor residing in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. In life, he worked for the wealthy Agamand dynasty at their extensive flour mills in northern Tirisfal. Convinced to stay and defend the estate against the Scourge, he died alongside his fellow laborers, and now dedicates his undeath to exacting vengeance on his former masters. Before the Third War, Coleman Farthing earned an honest living as a laborer at the Agamand Mills, the largest milling and agricultural operation in Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge poured across Lordaeron, the aristocratic Agamand family refused to flee their valuable lands. Instead, they urged their household and laborers to take up arms alongside them, promising they could hold the farmsteads against the undead horde. Coleman and his fellow workers stayed, believing their masters—a decision that cost every last one of them their lives. Raised into undeath only to break free under the banner of the Forsaken, Coleman harbors a burning hatred for the Agamands. Rather than blaming only the Scourge, he blames the sheer hubris and greed of his employers for tricking their staff into an impossible last stand. Now loitering in Brill's tavern, Coleman enlists Horde champions to march into the blighted mills, cut down the risen Agamand kin, and plunder the heirloom weapons housed within their family crypt so that the last of their honor is stripped away.

npc:dalar-dawnweaver.text: Dalar Dawnweaver. Dalar Dawnweaver is a former archmage of Dalaran who now serves the Forsaken at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Slain during the Scourge's destruction of the magi's city and later freed from the Lich King's control, he turns his magical intellect toward dissecting regional threats. From the shadows of the tomb, he directs efforts to understand Dalaran's lingering presence and undo the madness of Archmage Arugal. In life, Dalar Dawnweaver held high rank among the Kirin Tor, walking the halls of the Violet Citadel when Dalaran was a pinnacle of arcane mastery. His mortal life ended when the Scourge sacked the city to pave the way for Archimonde's summoning. Reanimated into the mindless thrall of the Lich King, Dalar broke free alongside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner when the Scourge's grip faltered. Now stationed at the Sepulcher, he retains the piercing intellect of an archmage, turned entirely toward safeguarding the Forsaken realm. Silverpine Forest is caught between multiple perils, and Dalar serves as the Sepulcher's arcane strategist. To the south, Dalaran wizards occupy Ambermill, meddling in matters Dalar seeks to uncover and disrupt. Even closer looms Shadowfang Keep and the feral worgen loosed upon the woods. Dalar possesses intimate knowledge of his former colleague, Archmage Arugal, and meticulously orchestrates campaigns to neutralize Arugal's beastly creations before they overrun the region.

npc:darsok-swiftdagger.text: Darsok Swiftdagger. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern trails for threats. The orc scout directs Horde fighters against Witchwing harpies in the Dry Hills, whose raids endanger travelers and settlements. He is also an old friend of Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin. Darsok Swiftdagger watches the northern scrubland from the Crossroads. The roads linking Durotar, Mulgore, and the Barrens’ northern reaches face raiders and centaur, as well as organized hunters from the sky. Darsok’s anger falls on the Witchwing harpies. Their roosts lie in the Dry Hills, northwest of the Forgotten Pools, where they threaten caravans traveling north. Darsok has an old friend far northwest of the Barrens: Witch Doctor Jin'Zil, a troll who lives at Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, the land the harpies come from. Darsok sends Jin'Zil a letter with news of the harpy campaign. The two friends have not been in touch for many years.

npc:deathguard-dillinger.text: Deathguard Dillinger. Deathguard Dillinger is a Forsaken sentry stationed in Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Standing watch over the town's perimeter, he directs newly arrived undead toward necessary services and tasks recruits with keeping the local Scourge remnants at bay. As a member of the Forsaken Deathguard, Dillinger stands at the entrance of Brill, serving as both a frontline protector and an orienting guide for travelers emerging from Deathknell. He provides directions to town amenities such as the inn, the town hall, and local trainers, helping newly awakened undead navigate their new reality under the Dark Lady's rule. Dillinger actively enlists capable adventurers to purge lingering mindless Scourge from the nearby farms and mills. Through assignments like cullling rotting ghouls and reclaiming infested facilities, he seeks to establish a buffer zone of security around Brill, ensuring the fledgling Forsaken settlements can endure against unending undead predation.

npc:dendrite-starblaze.text: Dendrite Starblaze. Dendrite Starblaze is a night elf druid residing in the sacred village of Nighthaven within Moonglade. Serving the Cenarion Circle, he acts as a vital mentor and guide for budding druids of both night elf and tauren descent. Through him, practitioners are summoned to the holy grove to master essential rites such as cleansing toxins and communing with nature's forms. Perched within Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze represents the nonpartisan, enduring spirit of the Cenarion Circle. When novice druids learn to attune their spirits to Teleport: Moonglade, Dendrite is among the first to welcome them upon arrival. He bridges the gap between ancient Kaldorei tradition and the emerging path of the tauren, treating all who heed the call of the wild as kin beneath the boughs of the sacred haven. Dendrite's primary duty involves initiating druidic apprentices into the deeper mysteries of nature. He directs novices through the trials required to understand poison and pestilence, sending them to examine tainted waters and discover herbal curatives. He also oversees the steps that lead druids to the water trials, testing their patience and endurance beneath the surface before granting communion with aquatic forms.

npc:devrak.text: Devrak. At the Crossroads, Devrak keeps the Horde’s wind riders ready for the roads across Kalimdor. The orc flight master carries couriers and supplies between Durotar, Mulgore, frontier outposts, and the Horde’s capitals. At the Crossroads, Devrak tends the wind riders that link the Horde’s far-flung holdings. The outpost stands where Kalimdor’s major trade routes meet, exposed beneath the sun and vulnerable to quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. Quick flights matter here. Devrak pairs seasoned travelers and new messengers with trained wind riders that cross the savannah and reach Mulgore’s mountains or Durotar’s stone canyons. Devrak also helps move supplies from the frontier. Barrens hunters bring in meat and pelts, and he helps send them to Orgrimmar’s cooking fires and Thunder Bluff’s tanners. He introduces new couriers to flight masters across the continents, keeping an aerial route open to the Horde’s heartlands. Devrak tends more than beasts at the Crossroads. When the settlement comes under attack, he calls enraged wyverns to strike intruders with venomous stingers and talons. His roost is a dangerous target for anyone who attacks.

npc:eitrigg.text: Eitrigg. In Orgrimmar, Eitrigg stands beside Warchief Thrall as a trusted advisor. A veteran of the First and Second Wars, he left the Blackrock clan’s Horde after its defeat and lived in exile. Now he helps Thrall guide the New Horde toward honor and shamanism. Born on Draenor among the Blackrock clan, Eitrigg fought for the Horde in the First and Second Wars. The battles and the Horde’s defeat in the second war forced him to face how far his people had fallen into bloodlust and demonic corruption. Sickened by what the Horde had become, he left its scattered remnants and sought solitude in the wilds of Lordaeron. During his exile, Eitrigg sheltered in an abandoned tower near Hearthglen. The human paladin Tirion Fordring found him, and their clash brought the tower’s ruins down around them. Eitrigg pulled the unconscious human to safety instead of finishing him. Moved by this act of martial honor, Tirion swore friendship and kept the hermit’s location secret. The local Alliance authorities eventually captured Eitrigg and sentenced him to hang in Stratholme. Tirion cast aside his knighthood, lands, and freedom to attack the city and rescue him. Their bond showed both warriors that honor could cross the hatred between their peoples. In Stratholme, Thrall’s newly united Horde raided the city during Tirion’s attempt to free Eitrigg and carried the aging warrior away. Meeting Thrall convinced Eitrigg that the orcs were casting off demonic corruption and returning to their ancestral shamanic heritage. He crossed the Great Sea with Thrall to Kalimdor and took a revered place in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Wisdom. Now Eitrigg advises the young Warchief inside Grommash Hold. He helps evaluate new recruits and shares the wisdom he earned, so the New Horde does not repeat the tragedies of the past.

npc:executor-arren.text: Executor Arren. Executor Arren is a high-ranking Forsaken officer stationed in Deathknell. He oversees the immediate defense and consolidation of the settlement as newly awakened undead emerge from their graves. Arren coordinates the local campaign against mindless Scourge zombies, feral beasts, and the encroaching zealots of the Scarlet Crusade. Standing resolute just outside the chapel in Deathknell, Executor Arren serves as the primary military voice for the nascent Forsaken within their awakening grounds. While the caretakers in the crypts guide newly raised undead through their disorientation, Arren directs their focus outward toward survival. Under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's banner, he organizes local operations to sweep away mindless zombies that threaten the village borders, establishing secure territory in the shadow of Lordaeron's fall. Deathknell is surrounded by perils far deadlier than confused fledglings. Under Arren's orders, scouts and initiates strike at the vicious arachnids inhabiting Night Web's Hollow and eliminate dangerous predators haunting the woodland fringes. By demanding decisive action from every capable hand, Arren tests the fortitude of new arrivals, ensuring only those capable of defending their second chance at existence remain in the service of the Dark Lady.

npc:executor-zygand.text: Executor Zygand. Executor Zygand is a senior Forsaken commander stationed at the town hall in Brill, overseeing defensive and military operations across central Tirisfal Glades. Reporting directly to the Undercity's high command, he coordinates the purge of Scarlet Crusade forces pressing into Forsaken territory. Positioned at the administrative heart of Brill, Executor Zygand coordinates regional defense for the Forsaken after their initial awakening in Deathknell. Serving as the direct superior to regional officers like Executor Arren and field sentries such as Deathguard Linnea, Zygand synthesizes scout intelligence and dispatches able recruits to safeguard Lordaeron's borders from encroachment. Zygand's primary military concern is the fanatic presence of the Scarlet Crusade, which infests outposts across Tirisfal Glades. Under his direction, agents are sent systematically to strike at Crusader scouts, encampments, and forward bases, ensuring the zealots never muster sufficient strength to threaten the approaches to the Undercity.

npc:gan-rul-bloodeye.text: Gan'rul Bloodeye. In Orgrimmar, Gan'rul Bloodeye trains warlocks beneath the city. In the Cleft of Shadow, Horde initiates learn darker demonic rites and how to bend voidwalkers and succubi to their will. Warlocks study out of sight in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. Warchief Thrall tolerates them in the new Horde, though Durotar's open sunlight is no place for their dark arts. The cavern gives shadow weavers, rogues, and fel casters room to study unmolested. From there, Gan'rul teaches rising practitioners of fel magic. Ambitious warlocks come to Gan'rul to learn dangerous summoning rites. Those seeking to bind a greater demon, such as a resilient voidwalker or a seductive succubus, must secure ritual components and learn the precise incantations. The summoned creature must be dominated before it consumes its master.

npc:gann-stonespire.text: Gann Stonespire. Along the southern Barrens road near Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire seeks retaliation for his people’s displacement. The tauren nomad’s tribe hunted on land now occupied by a dwarven excavation. Gann Stonespire camps beside the southern Barrens road after the dwarven expedition arrived from Ironforge and built Bael Modan. The surrounding land had been his tribe’s ancestral territory and hunting grounds. Dwarven miners drove the tauren from their soil with pickaxes, firearms, and heavy machinery, and refused peaceful overtures. Gann will not surrender his heritage quietly. He calls on travelers to strike back at the excavators.

npc:gazrog.text: Gazrog. At the Crossroads, Gazrog keeps watch over the Horde’s roads and supply lines. He calls on passing Horde travelers to face threats in the Barrens and search for lost patrols. Gazrog watches over the Crossroads and the roads beyond it. Marauders and beasts threaten the supplies moving through this isolated settlement, so he works with its defenders to keep cargo, coin, and couriers moving. The wilderness demands constant attention, and Gazrog depends on passing travelers to answer trouble beyond the outpost’s stockades. Gazrog’s watch extends across trails where raptors prey on travelers and quilboar clans ambush scouts. He coordinates responses to highway robberies, including the recovery of stolen Horde shipments. He also keeps track of missing soldiers, among them the grunt Dogran, who is injured and held by the quilboar.

npc:gornek.text: Gornek. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek oversees new orc and Darkspear troll recruits in Durotar. He receives those preparing to prove their worth to the New Horde. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek puts new Horde recruits through their first test of discipline. Warchief Thrall's order is clear: every youth and newcomer must earn a place through grit and perseverance. Gornek assesses those entering the valley, reads their introductory orders, and directs them to trainers around the compound. Whether an initiate carries an encrypted scrawl, a glyphic parchment, or a simple tablet, Gornek receives the credentials and sends them onto a harsh path of survival. The valley's arid canyons test battle skill and teach the New Horde's communal ways. Gornek keeps novices from lingering aimlessly, pointing them toward nearby scorpid burrows, feral boar dens, and veteran instructors. Those who survive the training grounds and slay the threats in the red rock gullies receive Gornek's final acknowledgment before he sends them out into Durotar's wider, perilous landscape.

npc:gunther-arcanus.text: Gunther Arcanus. Gunther Arcanus is an exceptionally powerful necromancer dwelling on an isolated island in Brightwater Lake. Slain during the Third War and raised into undeath, he managed to shatter the Lich King's mental grip entirely on his own. Long believing he was the sole undead possessing free will, he defended his retreat against all outsiders until discovered by the Forsaken. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Gunther was a promising apprentice among the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Alongside close friends Bethor Iceshard and Thule Ravenclaw, he studied the arcane arts, secretly delving into necromancy despite the Kirin Tor's strict prohibitions against dark magic. To commemorate their brotherhood, the trio once bound their apprentice wands together into a single heirloom. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Gunther perished to the Plague of Undeath and was raised into servitude. Unlike most who required the Lich King's power to weaken or Lady Sylvanas to break their chains, Gunther's raw arcane mastery and sheer willpower allowed him to shake off the Lich King's mental domination entirely by himself. Convinced that every other walking corpse remained a mindless thrall of the Scourge, he retreated to an island in Tirisfal Glades, surrounding himself with shambling guardians and cutting off all contact with the living and dead alike.

npc:high-executor-hadrec.text: High Executor Hadrec. High Executor Hadrec is the military commander of the Forsaken garrison stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. From this central crypt, he oversees defense against regional threats including the gnolls of the Rot Hide clan and investigates the disappearance of scouts across the zone. He serves as the primary officer directing Horde operations throughout Silverpine. Stationed within the gloom of the Sepulcher, High Executor Hadrec directs Forsaken military operations across Silverpine Forest. While Tirisfal Glades is firmly secured by the Dark Lady's forces, Silverpine remains fraught with peril, bordered by hostile Dalaran mages, feral worgen, and encroaching gnolls. Hadrec bears the grim responsibility of consolidating Forsaken territory and stamping out anything that challenges Undercity authority south of the capital. Much of Hadrec's immediate concern revolves around the Rot Hide gnolls and Fenris Isle. These undead-tainted beasts have infested the Dead Fields and the shores of Lake Lordamere, posing an unpredictable and vicious threat to Forsaken patrols. Hadrec dispatches agents to scour the decrepit ferries and rotting farmsteads for clues, determine what empowers the beasts, and prepare an outright strike against their island stronghold.

npc:islen-waterseer.text: Islen Waterseer. Beside the Tidus Stair, respected tauren shaman Islen Waterseer guides Horde initiates through the trials of water. She lives by a quiet fishing hut and teaches shamans to attune to water spirits as they seek their Water Totem. On the Barrens coast, Islen Waterseer keeps to the craggy Tidus Stair, where arid plains meet the Great Sea. Water spirits are raw and near along this shore. Islen chooses this quiet outpost over thunderous halls and busy cities, spending her days listening to the tides. Shamans seeking communion with water come to her for guidance. To know water, a shaman needs inner harmony and spiritual sight as well as study. Islen guides seekers in preparing the Water Sapta, a sacred brew that pierces the veil between mortal senses and elemental manifestations. She teaches that water can be unyielding and deep, yet fluid and restorative. Anyone who calls on its aid must show it great respect. Though Islen lives quietly on the coast, her spiritual ties reach across Kalimdor. She shares a close, enduring friendship with Greta Mosshoof, another wise tauren skilled in the restorative arts. Islen's knowledge of water's purifying nature reaches beyond the Barrens, bringing spiritual aid to lands afflicted by deep corruption.

npc:kadrak.text: Kadrak. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the northern frontier between the Barrens and Ashenvale. He directs dispatches and reinforcements into the contested forest, where the Horde fights the night elves. At the Mor'shan Rampart, Kadrak guards the main route between the Barrens and Ashenvale. The barricade marks a hard border: Horde-held plains lie to the south, and night elf-guarded woods stretch north. Kadrak keeps watch against Sentinels and hostile woodland creatures, holding the perimeter against incursions. Kadrak also handles military reports between the Barrens and logging camps deeper in Ashenvale. Couriers bring him combat reports from the Warsong Outriders, and he directs supplies and reinforcements to outposts such as Splintertree Post. Those who report to Kadrak are sent onward into the struggle for the forest.

npc:magatha-grimtotem.text: Magatha Grimtotem. Magatha Grimtotem is the matriarch of the Grimtotem tribe and the Elder Crone of Thunder Bluff. A formidable shaman and political schemer, she resides on Elder Rise while continually challenging Cairne Bloodhoof's vision for the tauren nation. Magatha rose to absolute authority over the Grimtotem through an arranged union followed by the sudden, fatal climbing accident of her mate. Operating from Elder Rise with her personal retinue and bodyguards, she stands as the undisputed political and spiritual leader of her reclusive tribe. Unlike Cairne Bloodhoof, Magatha preaches tauren dominance, viewing other mortal races as intruders upon Kalimdor who ought to be eradicated or swept aside. Despite her open disdain for non-tauren, Magatha was among the earliest advocates for admitting the Forsaken into the Horde. She claims the tauren can teach the undead spiritual balance and guide them toward reclaiming their humanity. In practice, however, Magatha collaborates directly with the Royal Apothecary Society beneath Thunder Bluff, consulting figures like Apothecary Zamah on practical alchemy and arcane relic studies.

npc:magistrate-sevren.text: Magistrate Sevren. Magistrate Sevren is the chief administrative official presiding over the settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Standing inside the town hall, he organizes early Forsaken defense and directs arriving champions to stabilize the territory around the Undercity. Operating from the town hall in Brill, Magistrate Sevren coordinates civil authority and strategic efforts in the lands just north of the Undercity. As new Forsaken step forth into Tirisfal Glades, Sevren assesses local crises and dispatches adventurers to restore order, secure ruined infrastructure, and suppress persistent threats lingering in the surrounding hills. Sevren's primary concerns center on the preservation and recovery of the Tirisfal dead. Local graverobbers, rot hides, and rogue undead disrupt burial grounds, threatening the emerging dominion of Sylvanas Windrunner. Sevren ensures that ancestral tombs—such as the Agamand Family Crypt—are reclaimed and that deserters or uncooperative forces do not subvert Forsaken authority in the region.

npc:mangletooth.text: Mangletooth. At Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth faces execution in a Horde cage and bargains with those who visit him. He offers knowledge of his rivals and Agamaggan's ancient lore in return for their help. Tauren hunters and orc sentries keep Mangletooth in a cage at Camp Taurajo. The captured Razormane quilboar awaits execution, but he still tries to sway his captors and visiting Horde adventurers. He urges them to strike at the enemies of his tribe, hoping to prove his worth or win his freedom. Mangletooth knows the religious history of his people. During the ancient War of the Ancients, Agamaggan's spilled blood gave rise to the Barrens' massive thorns. Mangletooth gathers red crystalline Blood Shards from fallen Bristlebacks and channels the lingering divine power within them, granting ancient blessings to those who help him.

npc:master-apothecary-faranell.text: Master Apothecary Faranell. Master Apothecary Faranell is the head of the Royal Apothecary Society, stationed within the depths of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. In life a respected Dalaran scholar, in undeath he directs the Forsaken's search for a devastating New Plague to eradicate both the Scourge and the living. Before the Third War, Faranell was an esteemed alchemist who spent decades studying alongside the learned mages of Dalaran. He spent his mortal days seeking cures, remedies, and potions to improve mortal health. When the Scourge plague claimed his life and he arose as a free-willed Forsaken, his former scientific curiosity curdled into cruelty. Retaining his encyclopedic intellect, he traded healing salves for catastrophic reagents, quickly becoming one of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's most valued researchers in the bowels of Lordaeron's fallen capital. Operating out of the noxious laboratories of the Apothecarium, Faranell coordinates the far-flung research of the Royal Apothecary Society. He oversees the construction of lumbering abominations and directs subordinate apothecaries stationed throughout Lordaeron and beyond. Every batch of strange venom, tainted blood, and cursed flora gathered by field researchers across the continents eventually passes through his vats for distillation and refinement.

npc:master-gadrin.text: Master Gadrin. In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin guides the Darkspear through exile and loss. The elder witch doctor once trained the tribe's priests and mages with Zalazane. Now he helps his people and seeks to break the dark curse over their home on the Echo Isles. Before the Darkspear reached Kalimdor, Master Gadrin guided generations of his people in the South Seas. He served as a witch doctor on the islands they called home, teaching the tribe's mystical ways. On the Echo Isles, Master Gadrin and the young witch doctor Zalazane trained the tribe's priests and mages together. Zalazane fell under the pull of the dark voodoo he sought to wield, and madness took hold. He enslaved the minds of his people and drove Vol'jin and the uncorrupted Darkspear onto the mainland of Durotar. Now in Sen'jin Village, Gadrin bears the grief of watching a companion become a tyrant. He works to lay slain tribesfolk to rest and end Zalazane's rule. Master Gadrin knows more of troll spiritualism and loa lore than almost anyone alive in the Horde. Scholars, shamans, and the Royal Apothecary Society seek his counsel on arcane and alchemical mysteries. When the Burning Blade threatens Durotar, or distant researchers need forgotten rites, Gadrin draws on what he knows. He can decipher the ancient tablets of Zul'Farrak and invoke Shadra the spider loa, then craft the bindings such a rite requires.

npc:mebok-mizzyrix.text: Mebok Mizzyrix. Mebok Mizzyrix is an enterprising goblin entrepreneur residing in the port town of Ratchet. Ever eager to turn bizarre wilderness reagents into profit, he hires passing adventurers to gather unusual flora and fauna from across the Barrens and beyond. His most notorious project involves concocting a commercial intellect-enhancing beverage out of raptor horns. Operating out of the bustling, neutral port of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic Steamwheedle spirit of relentless opportunism. While Ratchet caters to sailors, pirates, and merchants of all stripes, Mebok focuses his keen eye on Kalimdor's wilderness. Rather than mining standard ore or trading mundane cloth, he seeks out rare biological curiosities that he believes can be refined into highly lucrative concoctions and commodities. Mebok's premier commercial endeavor is a proprietary 'smart drink' intended to artificially boost the intellect of whoever consumes it. Convinced that the natural cunning and ferocity of local raptors stems from the horns crowning their snouts, Mebok commissions hunters to harvest intact horns across the Barrens. To him, ethics and taste take a backseat to raw market potential, so long as paying customers believe the brew delivers results. Beyond raptor-derived elixirs, Mebok maintains a constant demand for other bizarre specimens. From collecting volatile Deepmoss spider eggs to commissioning the retrieval of rare Blueleaf tubers buried deep within the brambles of Razorfen Kraul, his pursuits consistently push intrepid mercenaries into perilous territory. If an organism possesses strange properties, Mebok is certain there is a way to bottle and sell it.

npc:melor-stonehoof.text: Melor Stonehoof. Melor Stonehoof is a veteran tauren huntsman stationed atop Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. As a mentor in the ways of the hunt, he tests the tracking prowess and mettle of Horde hunters by sending them after the most dangerous predatory beasts across the Barrens and Thousand Needles. Perched upon the breezy expanse of Hunter Rise, Melor Stonehoof observes the plains below with a practiced eye. The art of the hunt is sacred to the tauren, entwined with survival, spiritual balance, and respect for nature's greatest predators. Melor ensures that those who carry bow and blade in the name of the Horde understand this balance, directing promising stalkers to master their craft through trials against legendary beasts. Melor challenges hunters to seek out legendary and elusive beasts that terrorize the wild. He directs trackers across the plains of the Barrens, from aiding the huntress Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads to pursuing Steelsnap, a cunning and vicious hyena in Thousand Needles. Through these trials, hunters prove they can outsmart and outfight the deadliest creatures of central Kalimdor. For those whose skills exceed the Barrens, Melor points toward far-off lands. He charges seasoned hunters with bringing down beasts of terrifying strength, including Deadmire, an ancient crocolisk lurking in the swamps of Dustwallow Marsh, and the savage yeti Frostmaw of the Alterac Mountains. Each hunt serves to test whether a stalker has truly mastered the Hunter's Way.

npc:menara-voidrender.text: Menara Voidrender. In Ratchet, Menara Voidrender teaches warlocks from both factions the dark arts. The human warlock shares her knowledge of demon-binding artifacts and arcane craft from a refuge in Kalimdor, far from orthodox authorities. Menara Voidrender works from Ratchet, the neutral goblin port in the Barrens. Many warlocks in the Eastern Kingdoms study in cellars or hidden slaughterhouses beneath their cities, but Ratchet keeps Menara away from the Kirin Tor, Stormwind's guards, and Orgrimmar's overseers. There, she can pursue occult studies in plain sight. She teaches any capable apprentice, whatever their faction, making her a rare meeting point for practitioners of the dark arts. Veteran conjurers know Menara as an authority on orbs that imprison and harness demonic spirits. She works with intricate reagents and guides apprentices through demanding rituals to make enchanted attire and binding implements. Her skill is known as far as Ironforge and the Undercity, and senior warlocks across Azeroth send their most promising students across the sea to seek her counsel.

npc:morin-cloudstalker.text: Morin Cloudstalker. Morin Cloudstalker is a tauren scout keeping watch along the road leading east from Bloodhoof Village toward the Barrens in Mulgore. Standing vigil over the plains, he monitors local trade routes and investigates the encroaching threats endangering tauren travelers. Positioned beside the dirt path winding east toward the Barrens, Morin Cloudstalker acts as both a scout and a guardian for travelers through Mulgore. The grassy plains here are usually peaceful, but the opening of trade routes and shifting territories have drawn opportunists and bandits dangerously close to the heart of the tauren homeland. Morin's scouts recently attacked and burned a Venture Co. caravan on the northern shore of Stonebull Lake. When goblin salvagers were spotted near the burned wagons, he sent adventurers to examine the surviving supply crates and learn what the Venture Co. was hauling.

npc:mull-thunderhorn.text: Mull Thunderhorn. Mull Thunderhorn is a tauren elder residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Deeply devoted to the Earth Mother and the balance of the land, he watches over the sacred water wells scattered across the plains. As outside exploiters threaten the region's lifegiving waters, Mull guides young tauren through the rituals required to cleanse the ancestral springs. Standing watch in Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn carries the weight of Mulgore's spiritual well-being. The nomadic tribes have gathered under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to establish a permanent home, yet their lands are already under siege by greed and reckless expansion. Mull serves as a spiritual anchor for the young braves stepping out of Camp Narache, calling upon them to safeguard the vital resources of their ancestors.

npc:orgnil-soulscar.text: Orgnil Soulscar. At Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar watches for threats within Durotar. He gathers intelligence and coordinates defenses against dangers to the young orc nation, especially the Burning Blade cult in the canyons. At Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar tracks hidden threats across Durotar. While grunt patrols watch for Alliance forces and centaur raiders, he looks for danger among the orcs themselves. Scouts bring him reports from across the region, and he searches them for signs of corrupt rituals and secret gatherings.

npc:shadow-priest-allister.text: Shadow Priest Allister. Shadow Priest Allister is a Forsaken priest stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Overseeing intelligence and tactical efforts in the region, he coordinates operations to monitor Dalaran's wizards and secure the borders of Lordaeron for the Dark Lady. Operating out of the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister directs Forsaken reconnaissance throughout Silverpine Forest. From this central crypt settlement, he tracks nearby threats ranging from renegade humans and beastly incursions to the arcane machinations unfolding around Dalaran. Allister's chief concern lies with the surviving mages of Dalaran, particularly those occupying Ambermill and probing across the borders. Unwilling to let the Kirin Tor entrench themselves in Forsaken lands, he dispatches agents to intercept Dalaran messengers, decipher arcane runes, and determine the wizards' long-term ambitions. Beyond his duties as a field strategist, Allister is a cynical philosopher of the shadow. He is the author of 'Holy Bologna: What the Light Won't Tell You'—a scathing treatise criticizing traditional holy doctrine. The text explores the harsh realities of undeath and how the Holy Light fails those discarded by life, a work that has somehow circulated as far afield as the ruins of Dire Maul in Kalimdor.

npc:shadow-priest-sarvis.text: Shadow Priest Sarvis. Shadow Priest Sarvis stands inside the ruined chapel of Deathknell, serving as one of the primary guides for newly awakened Forsaken. He introduces fresh corpses to their grim reality, directing them to purge mindless undead and gather intelligence on local threats. Under Lady Sylvanas's banner, Sarvis works tirelessly to shape bewildered undead into disciplined servants of the Forsaken. Within the shadowy chapel of Deathknell, Shadow Priest Sarvis waits for those who have just clawed their way out of the grave. The awakening of a Forsaken soul is jarring and horrific, with many immediately losing their minds to mindless frenzy or despondency. Sarvis acts as an anchor, giving purpose to the newly risen. He assigns new recruits to put down the shambling, mindless corpses roaming the cemetery and directs them to secure Deathknell's borders against the encroaching Scourge. Beyond acclimating new recruits, Sarvis oversees crucial local defenses against lingering threats in Tirisfal Glades. He coordinates the containment of Scourge forces probing Deathknell's perimeter. By directing novices toward vital intelligence and martial trials, Sarvis ensures that the town remains a fortified bastion for the Forsaken.

npc:shael-dryn.text: Shael'dryn. Shael'dryn is an inquisitive dryad residing beside the Moonwell of Purity, east of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. She serves as a vital contact for night elf scouts investigating forest corruption. She plays a pivotal role in aiding Astranaar's sentinels with cleansing relics to combat demonic and foul influences spreading across the wilderness. Stationed beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn keeps watch alongside the night elf sentinels guarding the eastern approaches of the forest. When corruption surfaces among the local wildlife or tainted relics threaten the land's harmony, her deep natural understanding allows her to guide adventurers through the steps required to restore spiritual balance.

npc:shenthul.text: Shenthul. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul trains rogues and serves the Shattered Hand. He directs covert work across Kalimdor and brings promising rogues into its ranks. Shenthul trains rogues in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. While warriors and shamans march openly across Durotar, he teaches stealth, ambush, and subterfuge. His students learn fieldcraft and lethal arts for work in Kalimdor's harsh wilderness and unforgiving politics. Shenthul speaks for the Shattered Hand, once an orcish clan and now the Horde's intelligence network and secret service. He describes it as a watchful presence across Kalimdor, investigating, judging, and carrying out its own sentences. Pragmatic and independent of shifting politics, Shenthul reminds outsiders that the Shattered Hand existed before Warchief Thrall took power and will endure after him.

npc:sputtervalve.text: Sputtervalve. Under pressure in Ratchet, Sputtervalve races to finish shredder research for the Tinkers' Union. Director Riddlevox holds him to crushing deadlines, and he hires adventurers to steal designs from the rival Venture Company. In Ratchet, Sputtervalve answers to Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union. The goblin engineer oversees shredder development and has found the work brutal. Modern mechanization moves fast, the Venture Company presses hard, and his own prototypes are few. With the deadline closing in, Sputtervalve fears admitting failure to the Union. He turns to a familiar goblin practice: stealing better designs from those who built them first. The Venture Company's drilling operation at the Sludge Fen, to the northwest, is Sputtervalve's chief target. Its latest shredders have interchangeable hands, refined control grips, and advanced inner workings, including the elusive samophlange. Sputtervalve sent his associate Wizzlecrank into the Fen for field research, but Wizzlecrank became trapped. Now Sputtervalve hires wandering mercenaries to recover the stolen technology and rescue his partner. Sputtervalve also helps with strange curiosities that pass through the Barrens. Adventurers sometimes bring him bizarre artifacts infused with corruption from the Wailing Caverns, such as a glowing shard. He knows the local landscape well enough to point them away from machinery and toward the isolated druids encamped above the caverns.

npc:strahad-farsan.text: Strahad Farsan. Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan teaches warlocks to bind demons. The human warlock lives in a stone tower in the Barrens, beyond the reach of ordinary Alliance and Horde politics. Students of fel magic come from Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and the Undercity to learn from him. Strahad Farsan keeps to a stone tower on the bluffs above Ratchet. The goblin port's neutral ground lets him practice dangerous summonings away from Alliance magistrates and Horde shamans. His acolytes gather around him as he studies the Twisting Nether, apart from the struggles over territory below. Strahad learned the danger of demonic binding firsthand. His first attempt to bind a felhunter nearly cost him his life, leaving him cautious and exacting. Despite being human, he has earned the respect of Gakin the Darkbinder in Stormwind and demonic scholars in the Undercity and Orgrimmar. Warlocks of either faction seeking to command felhunters or fiery steeds are sent to his tower.

npc:sylvanas-windrunner.text: Sylvanas Windrunner. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner is the Banshee Queen and supreme ruler of the Forsaken, holding court in the Undercity beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Once the brave Ranger-General of Silvermoon, she was slain and raised into undeath by Arthas Menethil before breaking free from the Lich King's grip. Now allied with Thrall's Horde out of mutual survival, she is fiercely dedicated to securing a future for her free-willed undead and exacting vengeance upon the Scourge. In life, Lady Sylvanas was the celebrated Ranger-General of Silvermoon, commanding the defense of Quel'Thalas during the Third War. When Prince Arthas Menethil marched the Scourge into the high elven kingdom to reach the Sunwell, Sylvanas fought fiercely to delay his advance. Frustrated by her resistance, Arthas murdered her, but denied her a clean death. He ripped her soul from her corpse and twisted it into a vengeful banshee, forcing her to serve the Scourge and assist in the slaughter of her own people. When the Lich King's magical grip fractured after the Third War, Sylvanas broke free of his dominion and repossessed her preserved body. Amassing other undead who had regained their free will, she overthrew the dreadlords occupying the ruins of Lordaeron, dubbed her people the Forsaken, and established the subterranean realm of the Undercity. Recognizing the precarious isolation of her people—threatened by Scourge remnants, zealous Scarlet crusaders, and suspicious human realms—she forged an uneasy alliance of convenience with Warchief Thrall and the Horde.

npc:telf-joolam.text: Telf Joolam. At the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, Telf Joolam guides Horde initiates through the trials of fire. The Darkspear shaman teaches them to commune with and command the volatile element. Telf Joolam tends the Shrine of the Dormant Flame among the crags overlooking the borderlands. Fire spirits demand sharp discipline and unwavering focus, unlike the calm certainty of earth or the patient depth of water. Telf prepares young shamans for trials that test their worth before the wild embers consume them. Under Telf's direction, initiates brew and drink a ritual Fire Sapta, opening their mortal eyes to the unseen elemental planes. He sends them up the rocky summits to face burning spirits. Those who earn the flame must respect its ravenous hunger and resist reckless pride.

npc:thork.text: Thork. At the Crossroads, Thork keeps watch over the settlement’s defenses. He sends Horde adventurers against raiders and works to keep supply routes open. Thork commands the defenses at the Crossroads, where roads link Durotar, Mulgore, and lands beyond. The town faces threats from every side. Quilboar raids, centaur attacks, and harpies on the prowl stretch his forces thin. Thork calls on capable travelers to meet dangers his guards cannot handle alone. Thork’s watch reaches beyond the Crossroads walls. He sends scouts and messengers north to the Mor’shan Rampart, where they report to Kadrak. The northern and eastern routes carry supplies through the Barrens. Keeping those roads open sustains the Horde’s presence across the scrublands.

npc:thotar.text: Thotar. In Razor Hill, Thotar teaches young Horde hunters the ways of tracking and taming beasts. He trains orcs and trolls who have left the Valley of Trials to face Durotar’s wildlife. In Razor Hill, Thotar trains Horde hunters for the wilderness of Durotar. New recruits learn the basics in the Valley of Trials, then come to him as they face more dangerous predators. He teaches marksmanship and the respect needed to live alongside and direct Kalimdor’s deadliest creatures, drawing on traditions passed down through generations of orcs. Thotar guides young hunters through the ancient art of taming beasts. He sends them into arid canyons to calm and bond with native creatures, including venomous scorpids, armored surf crawlers, and cunning boars. His instruction teaches Horde trackers to build a bond with nature rather than rely on force.

npc:thrall.text: Thrall. Thrall now rules from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar, Warchief of the Horde and ruler of Durotar. Once a human slave raised as an arena fighter, he freed his people, restored their shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to a new homeland. Thrall was born Go'el, son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka. Gul'dan's assassins murdered his parents when he was an infant, and human commander Aedelas Blackmoore found him and named him Thrall, meaning slave. At Durnholde Keep, Blackmoore raised him as an arena fighter and taught him human tactics. With help from his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall escaped. The Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar guided him away from demonic corruption and taught him to master the elemental spirits. Thrall became the first orcish shaman of a new generation. After the Second War, Thrall joined Orgrim Doomhammer to free the orcs languishing in Alliance internment camps. Doomhammer fell in battle and passed his black plate armor and mighty warhammer to Thrall, naming him Warchief. The mysterious Prophet Medivh brought prophetic visions, and Thrall led his people aboard captured human ships across the Great Sea. They reached Kalimdor and escaped the doom falling upon the Eastern Kingdoms. In Kalimdor, Thrall reshaped the Horde from a warmongering force into an alliance built on survival and honor. He rescued Vol'jin's Darkspear trolls and allied with Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren. With human and night elf forces, the coalition defeated the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal. Thrall then founded Durotar and its capital, Orgrimmar, named for his father and mentor. He keeps an uneasy peace with Jaina Proudmoore's Theramore while defending his fragile nation and weighing controversial alliances, including the Forsaken of Lordaeron.

npc:tonga-runetotem.text: Tonga Runetotem. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem watches the Barrens' oases grow sick. Sent from Thunder Bluff, the tauren druid studies a corruption harming the region's wildlife and seeks its source before the fragile ecosystem fails. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem studies the Barrens' changing land. His elders in Thunder Bluff sent him from Mulgore, and he knows the dry savannah well. Where travelers see scrub and predators, Tonga watches for signs of the land's health. Lately, those signs have turned troubling. He seeks travelers who can help him investigate the scattered oases, the heart of life across the savannah. Tonga bears the Runetotem clan name and the druidic heritage championed by Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. Hamuul keeps ties with the Cenarion Circle and studies in Moonglade's sacred groves, while scouts like Tonga serve on the frontier. Tonga draws on Moonglade's botanical wisdom to prepare healing salves and counter poisons. His work puts the young tauren druidic tradition to use within the fledgling Horde.

npc:turak-runetotem.text: Turak Runetotem. Turak Runetotem is a revered tauren druid trainer residing in the Hall of Elders atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. Serving as a trusted assistant to Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, he guides novice tauren along the sacred paths of nature and balance. Through Turak, young druids undertake foundational trials to commune with spirits and master animal aspects. Within the serene confines of the Hall of Elders, Turak Runetotem stands as one of the Horde's foremost druidic mentors. Renowned for his deep patience and balanced demeanor, he assists Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem in reviving the ancient druidic arts among the tauren people. Turak ensures that every aspiring druid honors the will of the Earthmother, teaching that physical power must always be grounded in spiritual respect and harmony with nature. When a fledgling druid is prepared to embrace animal forms, Turak directs them into the wider world. He initiates their communion with the Cenarion Circle, teaching the art of teleporting across Kalimdor to the sacred haven of Moonglade. Recalling the bewilderment and intensity of his own youthful audience with the Great Bear Spirit, Turak tests his students' courage by sending them to face Lunaclaw and obtain the strength of body and heart needed to walk the Path of the Claw. Turak's guidance expands beyond primal combat forms to environmental stewardship. He sends his disciples back to Dendrite Starblaze to learn about poison, and Dendrite dispatches them to a rash of animal poisonings near the Crossroads, a situation that surprises even Turak. Through these trials, along with the arduous rituals beneath the tides to awaken the aquatic form, Turak shapes novices into enduring protectors capable of healing Azeroth's deepest wounds.

npc:varimathras.text: Varimathras. Varimathras is a dreadlord of the nathrezim race who serves as the chief lieutenant and military advisor to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Forced to pledge loyalty to the Banshee Queen after suffering defeat during the civil war for Lordaeron, he now stands at her right hand in the Royal Quarter of the Undercity. Before the Third War, Kil'jaeden sent Varimathras and his fellow dreadlords to Azeroth as the Lich King's jailors, to make sure the spirit of Ner'zhul served the Legion's plans. Bound alongside his brothers Detheroc and Balnazzar, he oversaw the Scourge in Lordaeron while Archimonde invaded Kalimdor. When the Legion fell at Mount Hyjal, the triumvirate remained entrenched in the ruins of the Capital City, entirely unaware of their master's demise until Prince Arthas returned to drive them into hiding. As the Lich King's hold over his undead forces fractured, Varimathras attempted to coerce the newly freed banshee Sylvanas Windrunner into serving the dreadlords' new regime. Sylvanas refused, rallying liberated undead to crush Varimathras's outpost. Facing execution, the dreadlord fell to his knees and bartered for his life, trading tactical secrets and knowledge of his brothers' fortifications in exchange for survival. Sylvanas accepted, binding him to her service as a living weapon against his kin.

npc:vol-jin.text: Vol'jin. In Orgrimmar, Vol'jin advises Warchief Thrall while seeking a lasting home for his people. The Darkspear chieftain is a master shadow hunter. Vol'jin leads the Darkspear after his father, Sen'jin, dies on their ancestral island. Sea witch-worshipping murlocs and human forces nearly destroy the isolated tribe, but Thrall's orcs intervene and forge a deep bond with the trolls. After fleeing the ruined islands, Vol'jin pledges his people to the New Horde and brings them across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. The Darkspear settle in Durotar, but Zalazane's betrayal on the Echo Isles drives many refugees to the mainland at Sen'jin Village. Vol'jin spends much of his time in Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar, giving Thrall his strategic counsel and shadow hunter skill. From the orcish capital, he watches over the young Horde and works to reclaim his people's lands.

npc:yaw-sharpmane.text: Yaw Sharpmane. Yaw Sharpmane is an experienced tauren hunter trainer stationed in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. He guides young hunters venturing out from Camp Narache, helping them master the wild beasts of their ancestral plains. Positioned amidst the tents and fires of Bloodhoof Village, Yaw Sharpmane serves the Shu'halo as an instructor in the ways of marksmanship, tracking, and survival. Young hunters who have proven themselves in Red Cloud Mesa are directed to Yaw to hone their craft as they step onto the broader plains of Mulgore. Yaw's most essential role is guiding novice hunters through the ancient rite of taming wild beasts. He tasks initiates with bonding with the native fauna of Mulgore, testing their patience and respect for the natural balance before instructing them on how to properly care for and train a permanent companion.

subzone:agama-gor.text: Agama'gor. Agama'gor stands north of the road from Camp Taurajo toward Mulgore. Bristleback quilboar hold this encampment in the southern Barrens, keeping pressure on the nearby Horde outpost. Agama'gor is a Bristleback stronghold in the southern Barrens. Its huts, brambles, and crude totems lie close to Camp Taurajo. The quilboar threaten travelers moving between the Barrens and Mulgore’s grassy hills, and Horde scouts and hunters fight to contain them. Bristleback quilboar in Agama'gor carry crimson stones called Blood Shards. Mangletooth, an exiled quilboar held captive at Camp Taurajo, seeks these stones because of ancient beliefs about Agamaggan’s sacred essence. Horde adventurers raid the encampment for shards and trade them to Mangletooth for tribal charms.

subzone:agamand-family-crypt.text: Agamand Family Crypt. Tucked into the hills just north of Agamand Mills, the Agamand Family Crypt is the ancient resting ground of one of Tirisfal's wealthiest farming dynasties. Now claimed by the Scourge under Captain Dargol, its tombs have been ripped open, and the slumbering ancestors raised as mindless terrors. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held expansive estates across northern Tirisfal Glades, entombing their forebears within this hillside mausoleum. When the Plague brought ruin to the kingdom, the crypt fell into the clutches of Captain Dargol, an agent of the Scourge. Rather than letting the wealthy lineage rest in peace, Dargol employed dark necromancy to awaken the entombed skeletons and vengeful apparitions, transforming a sacred burial ground into an aggressive Scourge foothold right on the edge of Forsaken territory.

subzone:agamand-mills.text: Agamand Mills. Agamand Mills is a sprawling farm and windmill complex nestled in the northern heights of Tirisfal Glades. Once the proud estate of the wealthy Agamand dynasty, it has fallen into ruin and stands as the largest Scourge stronghold in the region. The wealthy Agamand family built their estate around a vast milling network across northern Tirisfal. When the Third War broke out and the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the patriarch Gregor Agamand refused to flee, fortifying the compound and convincing his retainers and laborers to make their stand. Their provisions and stone walls might have held, but their youngest son, Devlin Agamand, betrayed his blood. Devlin slaughtered the estate watchmen and let the walking dead into the sleeping quarters. Crippled from within, the remaining defenders were wiped out, and the family joined the mindless ranks of the undead. Today, the Agamand Mills are the most entrenched bastion of the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades, posing an immediate threat to the Forsaken realm. The rotting windmills now churn above infested fields of wights, zombies, and skeletal horrors. Beneath the estate, Captain Dargol commands the garrison from the deep Agamand Family Crypt, practicing necromancy to reanimate generations of Agamand ancestors. From Brill, Magistrate Sevren and the Deathguards wage an active campaign to clear the mills and purge the Scourge presence before it can march upon the Undercity.

subzone:ambermill.text: Ambermill. Ambermill is a fortified human settlement in southeastern Silverpine Forest, situated just southwest of Lordamere Lake. Once a quiet lumber village, it is now occupied by surviving wizards and apprentices of Dalaran. Their presence represents a dangerous outpost of human resistance on the southern borders of the Forsaken realm. Before the Third War, Ambermill was a quiet lumber town of little importance. In the chaotic aftermath of Lordaeron's fall, the surviving wizards of the Kirin Tor moved in and fortified the settlement. Dalaran spellscribes, conjurors, and apprentices now patrol its buildings and stables, using Ambermill as a forward redoubt against the undead.

subzone:apothecarium.text: Apothecarium. The Apothecarium is the southwestern quarter of the Undercity and the headquarters of the Royal Apothecary Society. Within these noxious laboratories, Forsaken alchemists labor tirelessly under Master Apothecary Faranell to concoct virulent plagues, toxins, and engineered horrors. It stands as the grim heart of Undercity's biological research, vital to Lady Sylvanas's campaign against the living and the Scourge. Occupying the southwestern terrace of the subterranean capital, the Apothecarium is a labyrinth of bubbling vats, dissection tables, and pungent chemical fumes. Led by Master Apothecary Faranell, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes this district to advance their understanding of mortality and rot. Here, alchemists and surgeons experiment on tissue grafts, vivisection, and the assembly of mighty abominations. Their overriding purpose, mandated by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, is the formulation of a new plague capable of eradicating both the Scourge and the lingering human presence across Lordaeron. Beyond grand military ambitions, the quarter serves as the premier center of practical alchemy and herbalism for the Horde in the Eastern Kingdoms. Initiates and masters alike gather beside toxic canals to distill concoctions, study botanical blights, and consult master practitioners.

subzone:bael-dun-digsite.text: Bael'dun Digsite. The Bael'dun Digsite is a dwarven excavation carved deep into the mountains along the western edge of Mulgore. Established by Prospector Khazgorm's team out of Bael Modan, the quarry is viewed by the local tauren as a direct desecration of their ancestral homeland and an insult to the Earth Mother. Perched on the mountain slopes of western Mulgore, the Bael'dun Digsite represents the southernmost reach of the dwarven Explorers' League expedition based out of Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Unconcerned with territorial borders or the spiritual traditions of the newly settled tribes, dwarven prospectors arrived with picks, shovels, and blasting powder to unearth ancient Titan relics buried beneath the plains. The Bloodhoof tribe viewed this invasive quarrying as an outright assault on the Earth Mother. Baine Bloodhoof initially urged caution and attempted to warn the interlopers away, but the dwarves flatly refused to abandon their trenches. Concluding that diplomacy had failed, the tauren resolved to break the expedition's tools and forcibly expel the miners before their destructive digging tears further into Mulgore's sacred earth.

subzone:bael-dun-keep.text: Bael'dun Keep. Dwarven forces hold Bael'dun Keep above the Bael Modan excavation in the southern Barrens. Under General Twinbraid, this imposing fortification anchors the Alliance's controversial presence in the region and brings it into violent conflict with the surrounding Horde territories. Bael'dun Keep rises over the Bael Modan excavation as the fortified military heart of Ironforge's presence in the southern Barrens. Dwarven architect Haggis Boatmurder designed the stronghold to protect the Prospectors and archaeologists searching the trenches for ancient titan artifacts. Ironworks and artillery arm its garrison, which keeps a vigilant watch, secures dwarven supply lines, and projects Alliance military power into Kalimdor's heartland. The keep and its adjoining digsite displaced the local Stonespire tribe of tauren from their ancestral home. Bael'dun remains a flashpoint in the Barrens, and nearby Horde outposts see it as a flagrant military intrusion. Gann Stonespire wages a personal war of vengeance against the invaders. Aggrieved tauren, opportunistic scouts, and suspicious outposts such as Camp Taurajo keep the fortress under threat of raids and sabotage.

subzone:bael-modan.text: Bael Modan. Dwarven crews blast into the red earth at Bael Modan, searching for Titan relics. Their fortified outpost has driven the Stonespire tauren from their sacred land and kindled a bitter fight. Bael Modan's walls guard Bael'dun Keep, siege cannons, gyrocopter landing pads, and a deep excavation pit. Dwarven prospectors came to Kalimdor convinced an ancient Titan facility lay beneath the red earth. Their blasting tore through sacred ground of the Stonespire tauren. The expedition answered no call to negotiate. Gunfire and explosives drove the tribe from its ancestral lands, leaving survivors scattered and vengeful.

subzone:balnir-farmstead.text: Balnir Farmstead. The Balnir Farmstead is a derelict estate in eastern Tirisfal Glades, northeast of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once a working farm of the Balnir family, the lands now lie ruined and infested by wandering Scourge that slip past the Bulwark. For generations, the Balnir family worked their homestead in the rolling hills of eastern Tirisfal, and their garden of snapdragons still blooms among the ruins. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War, the farm was overrun and its people lost, leaving the buildings to rot. In the wake of the Third War, the ruins serve as a foothold for mindless Scourge slipping past the Bulwark. Forsaken deathguards watch the farm warily, while Undercity magi harvest surviving snapdragons from the garden to test how deeply plague corruption has crept into the soil.

subzone:bandarion-keep.text: Bandarion Keep. Bandarion Keep is a fortified redoubt associated with Tyr's Watch, nestled in the western reaches of Tirisfal Glades near the Whispering Forest. Named in honor of Garek Bandarion, the outpost serves as an isolated bulwark amidst lingering threats across the woodland frontier. Its defenders contend with everything from hostile coastal murlocs to roving zealots and unstable undead. Situated near the secluded Whispering Forest in western Tirisfal Glades, Bandarion Keep stands as a solitary sentinel for the Forsaken. Named after Garek Bandarion, this stronghold is closely tied to Tyr's Watch. Quartermasters like Jorin Croge work diligently to keep the garrison supplied despite its remote and challenging position far from the bustling courtyards of the Undercity. Holding the keep is no quiet assignment. The outpost faces constant danger from Vile Fin murloc raids along nearby waters, probing skirmishes by the Scarlet Crusade, and stray, mindless Scourge thralls shambling through the gloom. Worse still are internal perils: certain paladins struggling to adjust to their unlife as Forsaken have succumbed to madness, turning their weapons against their own kindred.

subzone:beren-s-peril.text: Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a secluded mountain cavern tucked in the rocky hills southwest of Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. It serves as an entrenched redoubt for rogue Scourge loyalists serving the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, plotting against the nearby Forsaken. Tucked away high in the crags southwest of Ambermill, Beren's Peril consists of a shadowed cave and winding mountain path hidden from the main roadway. Following the devastation of the Third War, rogue Scourge undead under the command of the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw fortified this enclave. Rather than bowing to the Dark Lady or retreating north, Ravenclaw's thralls—regents, guardians, and drudgers—gathered here in secret to muster an assault against the Forsaken base at the Sepulcher. Their presence was uncovered by Forsaken scouts, turning the quiet cliffside into an active warzone for Horde operatives sent to eliminate the threat before an attack could materialize.

subzone:blackthorn-ridge.text: Blackthorn Ridge. At Blackthorn Ridge, Razormane quilboar guard the southern Barrens north of Razorfen Kraul. Brine, an orc shaman, keeps watch from a camp above a pool of unusually pure mountain water. Blackthorn Ridge rises beside Razorfen Kraul, its slopes crowded with dense thickets of sharp briars. The Razormane quilboar claim the ground as ancestral territory, using the thorny barriers to ambush outsiders and skirmish across the southern Barrens. Travelers seek out the ridge despite the danger, drawn to Brine, a hermit orc shaman. His camp sits above a spring famed across Kalimdor for its clear, spiritually pure water.

subzone:bladefist-bay.text: Bladefist Bay. Bladefist Bay opens onto the Great Sea along eastern Durotar, just beyond Orgrimmar's gates. Craggy bluffs rise above its shore, with Azshara's southern coast across the water. Bladefist Bay meets the Great Sea along Durotar's northeastern edge. Rocky cliffs rise above its treacherous surf, just east of Orgrimmar, the Horde capital. Across the water to the north, Azshara's ancient red cliffs and ruins mark the far shore. The bay forms a boundary between Durotar and the open sea. Kargath Bladefist gave the bay its name.
